prose_links.location: Benefits worth testing, adjacent paragraphs 1 and 2
prose_links.first_paragraph: The supplier reports that 20 volunteer legal-office staff drafted 25% faster over two weeks (S2). This is a reason to investigate drafting assistance, rather than a forecast for our team. There was no comparison group, and the demonstration did not measure classification accuracy, review effort, profit or firm-wide outcomes. Volunteer selection and the legal-office setting also limit transfer to an 80-person professional-service team. The full report and underlying data are unavailable.
prose_links.next_paragraph: Faster initial drafting could release capacity, but the useful benefit depends on the effort required to check and correct outputs. An assessment should therefore compare total task time and output quality against existing practice on comparable work. Released hours would remain capacity unless a separately evidenced route to cash savings or additional revenue exists; neither labor valuation nor realized financial benefit is supplied (S1–S2).
prose_links.judgment: The first paragraph limits the supplier’s initial-drafting result and identifies unmeasured review effort and financial outcomes. The adjacent second paragraph explains why those omissions matter to leadership and translates them into a comparison of total effort/quality and a bounded financial interpretation. The link is a reasoned dependency, not merely a connective word.

prose_links.location: Cost and operational conditions, adjacent paragraphs 1 and 2
prose_links.first_paragraph: At the planning assumption of $20 per user per month, licenses for 80 users would total $1,600 monthly, or $19,200 for twelve months (S1). These figures use the supplied dollar symbol; the currency code is unspecified. They exclude unknown taxes, contract terms, training and implementation costs and are not an authenticated supplier quote. A smaller assessment's license cost would depend on its participant count and terms; no evaluation budget is approved (S3).
prose_links.next_paragraph: Costs alone cannot settle whether a trial is feasible. No integration test or deployment owner is established, and records may contain restricted client information (S3). The assessment plan should define permitted test material, access controls, review responsibilities and a way to stop work if information-handling or quality concerns arise. These are proposed safeguards to assess, not an assertion of legal compliance or approval to release client records.
prose_links.judgment: The cost paragraph establishes an incomplete planning baseline rather than an approved trial budget. Its neighbor adds the other conditions necessary for feasibility and gives concrete proposed safeguards. This broadens the decision on an explained basis while retaining the distinction between scoping and execution.

conclusion_linkage.opening_main_claim: Leadership should sponsor scoping a bounded assessment of document assistance for the 80-person team.
conclusion_linkage.conclusion: The subsequent decision should consider measured end-to-end time, correction effort, quality, integration feasibility and full costs. Leadership could then decide whether a bounded trial is justified or whether existing practice remains preferable. The present evidence supports scoping that decision, with no procurement commitment or rollout date.
conclusion_linkage.judgment: The conclusion recovers the opening request and the earlier reasons: limited drafting evidence motivates investigation, total effort/quality defines useful benefit, incomplete costs and operational conditions prevent committing to a trial. Its criteria recur from the body; the existing-practice alternative follows the proposed comparison baseline. It introduces no claim of demonstrated net benefit or authorization.

checks.basis: All seven substantive paragraphs contribute to the same decision. The opening establishes scoping; the supplier paragraph assesses the potential benefit and its bounds; the next derives the relevant measurement; the cost paragraph establishes the planning baseline; the risk paragraph adds feasibility conditions; the ownership paragraph makes scoping actionable without inventing an owner or deadline; the closing paragraph collects decision criteria. Actual adjacent pairs are quoted in prose_links. There are no exhibits or appendices needing integration.
